---
title: Quickstart
description: "Sign in and read your first event in under a minute."
---

<Steps>
  <Step title="Sign in">
    ```bash
    curl -X POST https://your-deployment/api/v1/auth/request-code \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"email": "you@example.com"}'
    # {"message": "Code generated (email delivery disabled).", "dev_code": "482913"}

    curl -X POST https://your-deployment/api/v1/auth/verify \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" -c cookies.txt \
      -d '{"email": "you@example.com", "code": "482913"}'
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="List your events">
    ```bash
    curl https://your-deployment/api/v1/events -b cookies.txt
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Read the public program — no auth at all">
    Every event with a published agenda exposes a read-only program feed, which is what the five embeddable widgets (sessions, speakers, agenda, itinerary, gallery) are built on:
    ```bash
    curl https://your-deployment/api/v1/public/events/{event-slug}/program
    ```
    Returns approved sessions, their speakers, tracks, formats, and rooms — one consistent payload so every embedded widget shows identical data.
  </Step>
</Steps>

From here, the [API Reference](/api-reference) covers every endpoint — submission forms, evaluation plans, agenda scheduling, file uploads, communications, all generated directly from the deployed server's own schema.
